being overweight/obesity was positively associated with brain/CNS tumor, meningioma and glioma risks in females, while being overweight/obes was positively associated with meningioma risk in males.
overweight status and obesity were associated with increased risk of overall brain/CNS tumours, meningiomas, and gliomas in women and meningiomas in men.
obesity is associated with increased risk of brain/CNS tumors and meningiomas, particularly in females.

the potential link between obesity and the risk of brain/CNS tumors.
the association of obesity and the risk of brain/CNS tumors.
a potentially preventable risk factor for brain tumors, namely being overweight/obesity.

obesity may be associated with increased risk of brain/CNS tumors in females, but not in males.
obesity is associated with increased risk of overall brain/CNS, meningioma and glioma in females, and with meningioma in males.
overweight/obesity is a risk factor for meningiomas and possibly gliomas in females, and for meningiomas in males.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
obesity may be an important factor in the etiopathogenesis of meningiomas, whereas the respective role in glioma etiology remains to be further elucidated.
obesity may be a modifiable risk factor for meningiomas and brain/CNS tumors.
overweight status/obese females are particularly at risk for meningiomas and obese females are at risk for brain/CNS tumors and meningiomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
obesity is an important risk factor for brain/CNS tumors and that it should be taken into consideration in the etiological research of brain/CNS tumors.

obesity is a risk factor for brain/CNS tumors.
